objects.name: Volt Typhoon Critical Infrastructure Intrusion (AA24-038A)
objects.description: Hand-curated Attack Flow of PRC state-sponsored actor Volt Typhoon, reconstructed solely from joint advisory AA24-038A (CISA/NSA/FBI et al., 8 Feb 2024). Campaign-typical behaviour: edge-appliance exploitation, VPN/valid-account persistence, NTDS.dit domain compromise via vssadmin+ntdsutil, LOTL discovery, and pre-positioning toward OT assets without executing destructive action.

external_references.description: PRC State-Sponsored Actors Compromise and Maintain Persistent Access to U.S. Critical Infrastructure. CISA, NSA, FBI, with DOE, EPA, TSA, ASD's ACSC, CCCS, NCSC-UK, NCSC-NZ. 8 Feb 2024.
Text source used for this reconstruction (cisa.gov blocks automated retrieval).

objects.name: Gather Victim Org Information
objects.description: Extensive pre-compromise reconnaissance to learn about the target organization.

objects.name: Gather Victim Network Information
objects.description: Pre-compromise reconnaissance to learn the target's network topology and protocols.

objects.name: Gather Victim Identity Information

objects.name: Gather Victim Host Information
objects.description: Web searches for victim host information.

objects.name: Search Open Websites/Domains
objects.description: Uses FOFA, Shodan, and Censys to search for exposed infrastructure.

objects.name: Search Victim-Owned Websites
objects.description: Searches victim-owned sites for host, identity, and network information.

objects.name: Acquire Infrastructure: Virtual Private Server
objects.description: Multi-hop C2 proxy composed of virtual private servers (VPSs).

objects.name: Compromise Infrastructure: Botnet
objects.description: Cisco and NETGEAR end-of-life SOHO routers implanted with KV Botnet malware.

objects.name: Compromise Infrastructure: Server
objects.description: Converted a compromised PRTG server into a proxy for C2 traffic.

objects.name: Develop Capabilities: Exploits
objects.description: Adept at discovering and exploiting zero-day vulnerabilities.

objects.name: Obtain Capabilities: Exploits
objects.description: Uses publicly available exploit code for known vulnerabilities.

objects.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
objects.description: Exploits vulnerabilities in networking appliances (Fortinet, Ivanti, NETGEAR, Citrix, Cisco); one confirmed case exploited CVE-2022-42475 in an unpatched FortiGate 300D.

objects.name: External Remote Services
objects.description: Connects to the victim network via VPN sessions for discreet follow-on activity.

objects.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter
objects.description: Hands-on-keyboard execution via the command-line.

objects.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: PowerShell
objects.description: Executes FRP clients and scripts via PowerShell.

objects.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Unix Shell
objects.description: Brightmetricagent.exe CLI library can leverage PowerShell, WMI, and Z Shell.

objects.name: Windows Management Instrumentation
objects.description: WMIC commands execute ntdsutil to copy NTDS.dit and the SYSTEM hive from a shadow copy.

objects.name: Valid Accounts
objects.description: Primarily relies on valid credentials for persistence.

objects.name: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
objects.description: Obtains credentials from public-facing appliances by exploiting privilege-escalation vulnerabilities in the OS or network services.

objects.name: Direct Volume Access
objects.description: Executes the Windows-native vssadmin command to create a volume shadow copy.

objects.name: Indicator Removal: Clear Windows Event Logs
objects.description: Selectively clears Windows Event Logs to remove evidence. (v19.1: revoked -> T1685.005.)

objects.name: Indicator Removal: File Deletion
objects.description: Created systeminfo.dat in C:\Users\Public\Documents, then deleted it.

objects.name: Indicator Removal: Clear Persistence
objects.description: Clears system logs and other technical artifacts to remove intrusion evidence.

objects.name: Masquerading: Match Legitimate Name or Location
objects.description: Masquerades file names; downloaded comsvcs.dll to a non-standard folder.

objects.name: Modify Registry
objects.description: Uses netsh to create a PortProxy registry modification on the PRTG server.

objects.name: Obfuscated Files or Information: Software Packing
objects.description: Packed FRP clients and ScanLine with UPX.

objects.name: System Binary Proxy Execution
objects.description: LOTL / LOLBins: native tools and processes to maintain and expand access.

objects.name: Unsecured Credentials
objects.description: Obtained a domain-admin credential insecurely stored on the appliance.

objects.name: Unsecured Credentials: Private Keys
objects.description: Accessed the Chrome Local State file holding the AES key that decrypts stored passwords.

objects.name: OS Credential Dumping: LSASS Memory
objects.description: Used comsvcs.dll MiniDump with the LSASS PID to dump LSASS process memory.

objects.name: OS Credential Dumping: NTDS
objects.description: Extracts the Active Directory database (NTDS.dit) from the DC -> full domain compromise.

objects.name: Brute Force: Password Cracking
objects.description: Exfiltrates NTDS.dit and the SYSTEM hive to crack passwords offline.

objects.name: Credentials from Password Stores
objects.description: Harvests saved passwords, history, and cookies from browsers.

objects.name: Credentials from Web Browsers
objects.description: Targets network-administrator browser history and stored credentials.

objects.description: LOTL utilities for network-service discovery.

objects.name: Permission Groups Discovery

objects.description: LOTL utilities for user discovery.

objects.name: File and Directory Discovery

objects.name: Process Discovery

objects.name: Account Discovery: Local Account

objects.name: Internet Connection Discovery

objects.name: System Service Discovery

objects.name: Application Window Discovery

objects.name: Log Enumeration
objects.description: Captured successful logon events (Event ID 4624) via PowerShell queries.

objects.name: Query Registry
objects.description: Enumerated stored PuTTY sessions.

objects.name: Software Discovery
objects.description: Obtained the victim's list of installed applications.

objects.name: Peripheral Device Discovery
objects.description: Obtained screen dimension and display-device information.

objects.name: System Location Discovery
objects.description: Obtained the victim's system locale.

objects.name: System Time Discovery
objects.description: Obtained the victim's system timezone.

objects.name: Browser Information Discovery
objects.description: Enumerated browser history and stored data.

objects.name: Remote Services: Remote Desktop Protocol
objects.description: Moves laterally to the DC via an interactive RDP session with a domain-admin account.

objects.name: Remote Service Session Hijacking
objects.description: PuTTY profiles for water-treatment, wells, a substation, and OT systems would enable access to those critical systems.

objects.name: Remote Services: Cloud Services
objects.description: [Attribution inconclusive] anomalous login attempts to an Azure tenant.

objects.name: Use Alternate Authentication Material
objects.description: [May be capable] Pass-the-Hash or Pass-the-Ticket after full AD compromise.

objects.name: Valid Accounts: Cloud Accounts
objects.description: [Attribution inconclusive] Azure logins potentially using credentials stolen via NTDS.dit.

objects.name: Archive Collected Data
objects.description: Collected sensitive file-server information in multiple zipped files.

objects.description: Compressed extracted NTDS.dit and registry hives with ronf.exe (a renamed rar.exe).

objects.name: Data Staged
objects.description: Saved History.zip to the Downloads directory for exfiltration.

objects.name: Screen Capture
objects.description: Captured a screenshot using gdi32.dll and gdiplus.dll.

objects.name: Proxy
objects.description: FRP clients establish covert C2 channels; SOHO routers and VPSs proxy C2 traffic.

objects.name: Proxy: Internal Proxy
objects.description: netsh PortProxy modification on the PRTG server redirects port traffic.

objects.name: Proxy: Multi-hop Proxy
objects.description: Multi-hop proxies (VPSs / SOHO routers) for C2 infrastructure.

objects.name: Ingress Tool Transfer
objects.description: Downloaded an outdated comsvcs.dll to the DC in a non-standard folder.

objects.name: Encrypted Channel
objects.description: FRP clients open reverse proxies establishing covert (encrypted) C2 channels.

objects.name: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol
objects.description: Likely exfiltrated collected files via Server Message Block (SMB).

objects.name: Gather Victim Identity Information: Email Addresses
objects.description: Post-compromise: targets the personal emails of key network and IT staff, informed by harvested browser data.
A public-facing network appliance is unpatched and exploitable (one confirmed case: CVE-2022-42475 in a FortiGate 300D).

Volt Typhoon is pre-positioned on the IT network with the capability to reach OT assets; consistent with the advisory, no destructive OT action is executed -- the objective is long-term, stealthy persistence.
